subject: Post-call: ACME pilot scope — volume bands & latency/cost options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: sales_ops@acme.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & pricing options (pilot)

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a concrete set of options so we can lock next steps:

Summary of what you shared
- Expected steady-state: ~120M tokens/month; peak days ~6M tokens
- Concurrency/UX: ~30–50 concurrent users, interactive flows (p95 target ~350ms)
- Target budget range: $2k–$3k/month initially (you flagged $2–3k as the pilot budget band)

Key trade-offs we discussed (latency vs cost):
- Streaming / low-latency path: best for <400ms p95. Higher $/1M tokens due to less batching and reserved CPU/GPU slices. Example: ~"Streaming" estimate $28/1M tokens.
- Batch / micro-batching path: amortizes model compute across requests, lowers $/1M tokens (example: ~$12/1M) but typically adds 70–150ms median latency depending on batch window. Could still hit p95 if we tune.
- Dedicated reserved pool: for steady high volume, commit pricing drives unit cost down (example: $9/1M with monthly commit + modest setup). Best if you expect sustained >100M tokens/month and need isolation.

Quick cost math against your 120M token estimate (illustrative):
- Streaming (@$28/1M) => ~$3.36k/mo
- Batch (@$12/1M) => ~$1.44k/mo
- Dedicated reserved (@$9/1M) => ~$1.08k/mo + commit

Recommendation for pilot
- 2-week side-by-side: route 20% of traffic to Streaming tier (validate UX), 80% to Batch tuning. This gives real SLO measurements and token counts.
- Instrument token spend and sample latencies (we’ll provide a tracing hook + dashboard).
- If you want to strictly keep pilot spend <= $3k, we can cap Streaming traffic to 15% and extend pilot to 3 weeks to gather equivalent signal.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short pilot_scope.pdf and a mutual_action_plan.xlsx that outline milestones, instruments, and the rollback criteria.

Next steps
- Drop comments on the attached MAP (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) — I can update today.
- Let me know whether you want 2-week vs 3-week pilot and if your finance team needs a PO/initial invoice.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales_ops@acme.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pricing options (pilot)

Thanks, Naomi — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume: 120M/month is our conservative baseline for the first quarter post-launch. Could be higher if conversion lifts during surveys.
- Latency: true requirement is p95 <= 350ms for the primary interactive flow. We can tolerate occasional 500ms for non-critical flows.
- Budget: the $2k–3k is what I can get approved for a pilot; if it looks promising we have room to scale quickly.

We like the side-by-side idea. Two practical asks:
1) Can you provide a concrete cap plan so we don’t accidentally exceed $3k for the pilot? (e.g., throttles, % routing, or token caps).
2) Any quick wins to reduce token spend without hurting UX? We have fairly chatty prompts right now.

If you can get me a one-page cost projection (Streaming vs Batch vs Reserved) with the commit thresholds called out, I’ll share with procurement and finance.

—Alex
Alex Jenkins
Director, Product 
Acme Robotics
alex.jenkins@acme.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: sales_ops@acme.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pricing options (pilot)

Alex — great, thanks for the specifics. Attached I’m sending a one-page cost_estimates.csv (CSV attached) and an updated MAP with explicit throttles. Answers inline: 

1) Pilot cost cap options (we implement at infra level)
   - % routing cap: limit Streaming to 15% of requests (automated routing) — easiest to enforce.
   - Token cap: per-day token ceiling with automatic 429s once reached. We can set daily caps that map to your $3k ceiling.
   - Hybrid: allow a 10% buffer for debug days but hit hard token cap thereafter.

2) Quick wins to reduce token spend
   - Prompt tightening: remove redundant system/context at turn boundaries (we’ll share suggested prompt diffs).
   - Response length caps and smart truncation for low-risk flows.
   - Use batch for high-volume non-interactive background calls (e.g., nightly summarization).

Estimated unit economics (final depends on model choice & quantization):
- Streaming (interactive, low-latency): ~$28/1M tokens (hosted tier)
- Batch (latency-tolerant, tuned batching): ~$12/1M tokens
- Dedicated Reserved (commit 3mo+): ~$9/1M tokens

If you’re comfortable with the numbers, next step is I’ll:
- Send a formal pilot MPA (scope + cap options) — attached.
- If procurement needs a formal quote, I’ll loop Marissa to produce an approved quote + any short-term credit we can add.

Would you like me to cap Streaming at 15% for the pilot and set a conservative token cap that maps to $3k?

Naomi
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: FW: ACME pilot pricing ask — potential discount?

Marissa — forwarding the thread. ACME is a neat fit: 120M baseline, strong chance to expand. They asked for a one-pager and a hard cap mapping to $3k.

Points for ops/pricing:
- Pilot revenue at full list pricing (Streaming mix 15%) would land ~2.1–2.9k depending on splits. If they convert to Dedicated we could see long-term >$2k/mo committed.
- They asked if any promotional credit or 20% pilot discount is possible to keep initial spend within $3k while giving them enough Streaming signal.
- If we offer a discount, we should require a 30-day technical pilot MPA and a post-pilot ROI review; include rollback clause.

Can you advise what one-off credit we can offer for a mid-market account in this band? If you want, I’ve attached the pilot MAP and cost estimates (pilot_scope.pdf, cost_estimates.csv).

Thanks — Naomi
